clue.text: Calm, swallowing drink (no ice), from dawn to dusk

indicators.note: one word swallowing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to allay fears is to calm them

indicators.note: no tells us to leave out the next word's letters from the drink

parts.note: taken as the word itself, before part of it is dropped
a rink is a sheet of ice for skating

explanation.surface: A soothing scene: someone calm, sipping a drink without ice, from morning to night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ice' looks like a cube in the glass; here it is the rink, whose letters 'no' strips from the drink, leaving a single letter for 'swallowing' to take in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting from sunrise until sunset is the whole length of the daytime, an idiom for continuously.

clue.text: Contemptuously dismiss our flu, caught too badly

indicators.note: badly signals the preceding words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone caught flu badly, a medical story of misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges OUR, FLU, CAUGHT and TOO, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to treat a claim as so absurd it is not worth hearing, as a judge dismissing a case with derision.

clue.text: Attendee not originally disturbed in accommodation

indicators.note: disturbed means the remaining letters are jumbled
not originally means losing the opening letter of the guest's word

parts.note: taken as written, before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A guest at a hotel is disturbed in their room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not originally' drops the first A from ATTENDEE, and 'disturbed' rearranges TTENDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Political easing of tension between rival states is a mutual accommodation, a diplomatic synonym.

clue.text: Empty young, good bar that's filled with sulphur and ash

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters, the contents removed

parts.note: GD is a standard abbreviation for good

indicators.note: filled with tells us the bar contains the next letter

parts.note: a rail is a bar
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A grimy bar for the young, filled with sulphurous fumes and ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' keeps only the outer letters; 'filled with' puts the sulphur symbol inside the bar. In Norse myth the world is held up by a giant ash tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the world tree is an enormous ash, so the tree is an example of that species.

clue.text: Quiet parking places supplied with old magazines

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: the parking places are supplied with a letter placed among them

parts.note: lay-bys are roadside places to pull in and park in Britain

explanation.surface: Quiet lay-bys stocked with old magazines, a dodgy roadside picture.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside stopping bay; 'supplied with' puts O inside LAYBYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Playboy is a famous men's magazine title, so its plural names copies of such periodicals.

clue.text: River to computer is a different one

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
taken as written
a Mac is an Apple computer

explanation.surface: Someone attaching a river to a computer, a baffling instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River' supplies PO, so the definition is the closing phrase: the answer is another river, not the Po.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac flows through Washington DC, so it is a river distinct from the Italian one in the wordplay.

clue.text: Has lost on points, looking shocked

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and are rearranged

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: A boxer who has lost on points looks shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' rearranges HAS into ASH, followed by the compass points E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Shock drains the colour from a face, so a pale grey complexion is the look of someone stunned.

clue.text: Singer wants lute to play in piece

indicators.note: in places the jumbled lute inside the piece

parts.note: a bit is a piece

indicators.note: to play hints at the instrument's letters being moved around

explanation.surface: A singer wants a lute to play in their set piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' looks like a person; in crosswords it is often a songbird. 'to play' scrambles the instrument and 'in' sets it inside the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Songbirds are called singers in crosswords; this small blue-and-yellow bird is a common garden songbird.

clue.text: A number wanting mustard on sandwich

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another comes first

parts.note: mustard is a shade of yellow
a submarine is a long sandwich, a sub

explanation.surface: A diner order: one number wanting mustard on their sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like an order on a menu; it is a song, the Beatles hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is often called a number, and this is a well-known Beatles track.

clue.text: Make every effort in one area to separate two others that may 26

indicators.note: the letter sits between the two other words to separate them

parts.note: a bust and a gut are both body parts that may stand out (the answer to 26)
a bust and a gut are both body parts that may stand out (the answer to 26)
A stands for area, and for one

explanation.surface: Straining in one region, between two body parts that bulge.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is STAND OUT: a bust and a gut both protrude. A goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for straining yourself to the limit, trying extremely hard.

clue.text: Without a smile, sacrificing daughter for husband regularly

indicators.note: sacrificing one letter for another means swapping them

parts.note: dourly means in a stern, unsmiling way
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A grim spouse who regularly gives up a child for her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacrificing daughter for husband' replaces the D of DOURLY with H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens every hour happens at regular intervals, so the sense is periodic.

clue.text: Spare item is short

indicators.note: is short means the word is cut, missing its last letter

parts.note: a thing is an item

explanation.surface: A spare item is in short supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is short' drops the final G of THING.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective means lean or slender, with no excess flesh.

clue.text: To interrupt collapse, a minute's thought

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the small piece is placed within the larger

parts.note: ruination is total collapse
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: Stopping a collapse takes a minute's thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' here is the long noun for ruin, not the verb; 'To interrupt' breaks it open after its second letter for the minute's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminating is chewing things over mentally, so the noun means deep thought or reflection.

clue.text: Sounds like a son of Israel's an artist

indicators.note: sounds like signals a word spoken that matches another

parts.note: Reuben was the eldest son of Jacob, who was renamed Israel; the possessive gives Reuben's

explanation.surface: A claim that some biblical figure's name echoes a painter's.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob, also called Israel, had twelve sons; Reuben was the firstborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was the great Flemish Baroque painter, a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: Good manners in trial scene? Yes, sort of

parts.note: a court is where a trial takes place

indicators.note: sort of suggests sorting, i.e. rearranging the letters of the word before

explanation.surface: Politeness on display in a courtroom drama, grudgingly agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes, sort of' reads as a hesitant agreement, but 'sort of' rearranges the word yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite, considerate behaviour towards others is a synonym for good manners.

clue.text: Showing no 14, soldier holds up gun shooting everyone

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece below holds up the pieces above it
shooting implies the gun's letters are scattered

parts.note: all means everyone
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A rude gunman, a soldier holding up and shooting everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the answer to 14-across, good manners. 'shooting' scrambles gun; a soldier ant 'holds up' the rest because in a down entry it sits beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant man is courteous and chivalrous, so the negative means discourteous or lacking good manners.

clue.text: I start to cry and implore piteously

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word
piteously suggests a distraught, jumbled pleading, so the word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone begins to weep and begs pitifully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to cry' gives C; 'piteously' rearranges IMPLORE into OMPILER. 'I' is the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword setter, writing in the first person, refers to themself as the puzzle's maker.

clue.text: Hurry along to get TV working?

definitions.meaning: to continue quickly and determinedly, pushing forward
a joke reading: push the on button to switch the set on

explanation.surface: Someone in a rush to get the television going.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means continuing with urgency, and literally pushing the power button switches a set on.

clue.text: Olympic diplomacy avoiding this being read?

definitions.note: the phrase means a stern warning, which tactful handling avoids

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Diplomacy at the Olympics prevents a stern warning.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, reading the Riot Act means a severe reprimand; the 1714 Act was read aloud to disperse crowds. Tact is how to avoid it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactful behaviour avoids the need for a formal dressing-down, the idiom this phrase completes.

clue.text: Great man, one out and about the bank

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other

parts.note: someone who is out is openly gay
TSB is a British high-street bank, the Trustee Savings Bank

explanation.surface: A notable man, openly out and about near the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: TSB is a British high-street bank, and 'out' means openly gay. The great man is F. Scott Fitzgerald's title character.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitzgerald's title character is called the Great Gatsby, so he is one man known as great.

clue.text: Rise from bed to dismiss assembly

definitions.meaning: to get up in the morning
to expel or throw someone out
the number of people who gather for an event

explanation.surface: Getting up early to break up a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means getting up or evicting, and the noun means the attendance at a gathering.

clue.text: Flyer: "Dog left on unstable slope"

indicators.note: in an across entry, dog and left placed on the slope come after it

parts.note: scree is loose rock on a mountainside
a chow is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A warning notice: a dog left on a slippery slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet with the quote printed on it; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This owl, named for its shrill call, is a bird, and so something that flies.

clue.text: Such a positive attitude the makings of a small company?

definitions.text: the makings of a small company?
definitions.meaning: the abbreviation for company is made of a C and an O

explanation.surface: An upbeat mindset is what builds a small business.
explanation.walkthrough: CO, short for company, is made of two letters joined by a conjunction when spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective describes a confident, ready-to-tackle-anything outlook.

clue.text: Bring up — this?

parts.note: to bring up a child is to raise it, and what brings up a procession is its back end

explanation.surface: A question about raising something.
explanation.walkthrough: One word means both to raise children and the back, which is what you are when you bring up the procession's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to raise or nurture, and the noun is the back, where whoever brings up a line stands.

clue.text: No tailback in city

indicators.note: back means the whole phrase is read in reverse order

parts.note: a scut is a short tail, like a rabbit's

explanation.surface: No tailbacks in town: a traffic report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailback' looks like a traffic queue; it splits into 'tail', a rabbit's short scut, and 'back', which reverses the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucson is a city in Arizona in the south-western United States.

clue.text: An organisation starts to make intelligent criticism of body's structure

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, the same as an
NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A group begins to offer smart critique of the body's make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes M, I, C from 'make intelligent criticism'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the study of bodily structure, so the adjective means relating to that structure.

clue.text: Man with hesitation abandoning British project

parts.note: Stan is a man's name

indicators.note: abandoning means the following letter is dropped from the word before

parts.note: doubt is hesitation

explanation.surface: A man, hesitant, quits a British venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' is the verb, to jut out, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to protrude, sticking out beyond a surface.

clue.text: Fasten number on back of vest

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of the following word

parts.note: ether is an anaesthetic, something that numbs: a number

explanation.surface: Pinning a race number on the back of a runner's vest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs: ether. 'on' puts it after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up an animal with a rope is to fasten it in place.
